claim: Dendra2 is an initially green-emitting fluorescent protein that upon 405 nm illumination converts into a red-emitting form.
source: Dendra2 (Gurskaya et al., 2006) is an initially green-emitting fluorescent protein that upon 405 nm illumination converts into a red-emitting form (Chudakov et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Gurskaya et al., 2006; Chudakov et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2007).

claim: Dendra2's favorable photo-physics and low aggregation propensity make it optimal for super-resolution imaging purposes.
source: Dendra2's favorable photo-physics (Lee et al., 2012) and low aggregation propensity (Landgraf et al., 2012) make it optimal for our purposes.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Lee et al., 2012; Landgraf et al., 2012).

claim: In the experiments, only molecules that are immobile within a 60 ms temporal window are detected and represented in live cell super-resolution data.
source: In our experiments (acquired with a 60 ms frame rate), only molecules that are immobile within this 60 ms temporal window are detected and represented in live cell super-resolution data; fast diffusive molecules are motion-blurred and are not represented.
evidence: This is a methodological description of how the experimental approach works, based on the technical limitations of the imaging method.

claim: Photo-converted Dendra2 molecules typically remain in the emitting state for tens to hundreds of milliseconds.
source: The photo-converted Dendra2 molecules typically remain in the emitting state for tens to hundreds of milliseconds, and therefore a single molecule may appear in multiple frames and hence may be detected more than once.
evidence: This is based on the known photophysical properties of Dendra2 and observations from the experiments.

claim: Intermittent photo-physical blinking transitions complicate direct conversion from counts of detections into exact numbers of molecules.
source: These intermittent photo-physical blinking transitions complicate direct conversion from counts of detections into exact numbers of molecules (Lee et al., 2012; Rollins et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Lee et al., 2012; Rollins et al., 2015) and describes a known technical challenge.

claim: The raw number of detections is used as the metric in quantitative super-resolution analyses to avoid propagation of counting error.
source: To avoid propagation of counting error, we use the raw number of detections as our metric in quantitative super-resolution analyses.
evidence: This is a methodological decision made by the authors based on the technical limitations described.

claim: Regions of high local protein concentration will have a higher frequency of detections compared to regions of low protein concentration.
source: Regions of high local protein concentration will have a higher frequency of detections compared to regions of low protein concentration.
evidence: This is a principle underlying the time-correlated detection counting method, based on the physics of the imaging approach.

claim: Super-resolution images of Pol II in live cell nuclei show high local concentrations of Pol II molecules appearing as bright regions.
source: We obtained super-resolution images of Pol II in live cell nuclei (Figure 1B). High local concentrations of Pol II molecules appear as bright regions in the super-resolution images.
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The distinct bright foci in super-resolution images are interpreted as Pol II clusters.
source: We interpret the distinct bright foci as Pol II clusters (Cisse et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed data, supported by a citation to previous work (Cisse et al., 2013).

claim: Pair-correlation PALM analysis confirmed that the apparent spatial clusters reflected clustering of multiple molecules, rather than stochastic blinking of single molecules.
source: We confirmed that the apparent spatial clusters reflected clustering of multiple molecules, rather than stochastic blinking of single molecules, by performing spatial pair-correlation PALM analysis as previously published (Sengupta et al., 2011) (see Appendix 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the pair-correlation analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C and cited methodology (Sengupta et al., 2011).

claim: The time traces of representative Pol II clusters show evidence for rapid cluster assembly characterized by a steep, sudden inflection in the slope of the cumulant.
source: The time traces of representative Pol II clusters show evidence for rapid cluster assembly characterized by a steep, sudden inflection in the slope of the cumulant, arising from an increase in the frequency of detections (black arrows in Figure 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by the time trace data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: De novo cluster assembly events are interpreted as those in which the onset of slope increase occurs after the acquisition has started.
source: We interpret as de novo cluster assembly, events in which the onset of slope increase occurs after the acquisition has started (i.e. after time t = 0).
evidence: This is a definition provided by the authors for interpreting their data.

claim: Steep slopes in time traces are followed by an abrupt plateau due to a sudden decrease in detection frequency with virtually no Pol II detection events.
source: Steep slopes are followed by an abrupt plateau, due to a sudden decrease in detection frequency with virtually no Pol II detection events.
evidence: This is a description of the observed data patterns in the time traces.

claim: The inflection points with sudden transitions from very high to very low frequency of detections are interpreted as cluster disassembly events.
source: We interpret the inflection points with sudden transitions from very high to very low frequency of detections as cluster disassembly events.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed data patterns.

claim: Monte Carlo simulations of the tcPALM method corroborate the interpretations of the time trace.
source: The interpretations of the time trace are corroborated by Monte Carlo simulations of the tcPALM method (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The temporal analyses of Pol II data in live MEFs show transient Pol II clusters.
source: The temporal analyses of Pol II data in live MEFs (Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D) show transient Pol II clusters.
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1C,D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The signatures of stable Pol II clusters in fixed cells feature a large positive slope from the start of acquisition, indicating existence of the cluster before acquisition.
source: In contrast to de novo assembly, the signatures of stable Pol II clusters in fixed cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E) feature a large positive slope from the start of acquisition, indicating existence of the cluster before acquisition.
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E.

claim: H2B-Dendra2 proteins displayed gradual monotonic slopes from the beginning of acquisition expected for tcPALM analysis of stable structures, even when imaged in living cells.
source: Imaged in identical conditions as Pol II, H2B-Dendra2 proteins displayed the gradual monotonic slopes from the beginning of acquisition expected for tcPALM analysis of stable structures, even when imaged in living cells (see Appendix 2 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F,G.

claim: Time-correlated super-resolution analysis is readily able to discriminate between stable and transient protein assemblies.
source: This confirms that time-correlated super-resolution analysis is readily able to discriminate between stable and transient protein assemblies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of H2B and Pol II data.

claim: The live cell time traces of Pol II clusters in MEF are not consistent with stable clusters, and rather reflect clusters that are rapidly assembled and disassembled.
source: To summarize, the live cell time traces of Pol II clusters in MEF are not consistent with stable clusters, and rather reflect clusters that are rapidly assembled and disassembled.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the comparison of different experimental conditions.

claim: The apparent cluster lifetime (τcluster) is defined as the duration from slope onset to the subsequent plateau in the cumulant graphs.
source: From the observed time traces, we define the apparent cluster lifetime (τcluster) as the duration from slope onset to the subsequent plateau in the cumulant graphs.
evidence: This is a definition provided by the authors for their analysis.

claim: An average cluster lifetime of 8.3 (± 0.2) s was obtained from analyzing time traces of 214 Pol II clusters pooled from 6 live MEF cells under normal growth conditions.
source: We analyzed time traces of 214 Pol II clusters pooled from 6 live MEF cells under normal growth conditions, and obtained an average cluster lifetime of 8.3 (± 0.2) s (Figure 1E and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by the quantitative analysis shown in Figure 1E and the source data.

claim: The average cluster lifetime is independent of the excitation laser power.
source: The average cluster lifetime is independent of the excitation laser power, corroborating the conclusion that the measured lifetime is due to transient cluster dynamics and not single molecule photo-bleaching (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Under normal growth condition, the Pol II clusters in MEFs are very short-lived.
source: Thus, under normal growth condition, the Pol II clusters in MEFs are very short-lived.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the measured cluster lifetime of ~8 seconds.

claim: The observed seconds-long lifetime of Pol II clusters in the murine cell line is comparable to an earlier study showing a Pol II cluster lifetime of 5.1 (± 0.4) s in human cells.
source: The observed seconds-long lifetime of Pol II clusters in the murine cell line is comparable to our earlier study showing a Pol II cluster lifetime of 5.1 (± 0.4) s in human cells (Cisse et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim compares the current findings to previously published work (Cisse et al., 2013).

claim: The MS2 hairpin structure in the mRNA is specifically recognized by the coat protein of bacteriophage MS2 (MCP), which is exogenous to mammals.
source: This hairpin is specifically recognized by the coat protein of bacteriophage MS2 (MS2 Coat Protein, MCP), which is exogenous to mammals (Bertrand et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Bertrand et al., 1998).

claim: The accumulation of MCP-HaloTag on the mRNA enables imaging of individual β-actin mRNA molecules.
source: The accumulation of MCP-HaloTag on the mRNA enables imaging of individual β-actin mRNA molecules (Lionnet et al., 2011a).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Lionnet et al., 2011a).

claim: When multiple nascent mRNAs are synthesized at the β-actin gene loci, a bright accumulation of MCP-HaloTag signal is observed at the gene loci.
source: When multiple nascent mRNAs are synthesized at the β-actin gene loci, a bright accumulation of MCP-HaloTag signal is observed at the gene loci.
evidence: This is a description of the expected signal based on the MS2/MCP system.

claim: In response to serum induction, prominent foci of JF646 fluorescence are observed, consistent with sites of nascent RNA transcription.
source: In response to serum induction (see Materials and methods), prominent foci of JF646 fluorescence are observed (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), consistent with sites of nascent RNA transcription as previously described (Lionnet et al., 2011a).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, and cited work (Lionnet et al., 2011a).

claim: In living cell nuclei, up to four β-actin gene loci are observed.
source: In living cell nuclei, we observe up to four such loci (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B); this is consistent with the previous observation that the immortalized MEF cells are tetraploid.
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The observation of up to four β-actin gene loci is consistent with the previous observation that the immortalized MEF cells are tetraploid.
source: In living cell nuclei, we observe up to four such loci (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B); this is consistent with the previous observation that the immortalized MEF cells are tetraploid.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison to previous observations about the cell line.

claim: The Dendra2-Pol II expression did not change the MS2 knocked-in β-actin gene levels in any apparent way.
source: The Dendra2-Pol II expression therefore did not change the MS2 knocked-in β-actin gene levels in any apparent way (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), nor did it affect transcription dynamics in response to serum (Lionnet et al., 2011a; Kalo et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and citations (Lionnet et al., 2011a; Kalo et al., 2015).

claim: Dendra2-Pol II expression did not affect transcription dynamics in response to serum.
source: The Dendra2-Pol II expression therefore did not change the MS2 knocked-in β-actin gene levels in any apparent way (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), nor did it affect transcription dynamics in response to serum (Lionnet et al., 2011a; Kalo et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Lionnet et al., 2011a; Kalo et al., 2015).

claim: Merging the two super-resolved images reveals that Pol II clusters co-localized with the β-actin gene.
source: Merging the two super-resolved images, we observe that Pol II clusters co-localized with the β-actin gene (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the merged image shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The localization accuracies measured based on the detected Dendra2 and JF646 fluorescence are 31 nm and 18 nm respectively.
source: The localization accuracies measured based on the detected Dendra2 and JF646 fluorescence are 31 nm and 18 nm respectively (see Appendix 3 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–I).
evidence: The claim is supported by the measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D–I.

claim: Within the super-resolution localization accuracy, Pol II molecules do cluster on the actively transcribed β-actin gene in living cells.
source: Within our super-resolution localization accuracy, we conclude that Pol II molecules do cluster on the actively transcribed β-actin gene in living cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the co-localization data and localization accuracy measurements.

claim: The Pol II clusters co-localizing with the transcribed β-actin gene are short-lived (6.3 s in the example represented).
source: As illustrated by the example in Figure 2F, the Pol II clusters are short-lived (6.3 s in the example represented), consistent with our global observation of short-lived Pol II clusters throughout the nucleus (as in Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the time trace data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Transient Pol II clusters occur, at least in part, on active gene loci.
source: Therefore transient Pol II clusters occur, at least in part, on active gene loci.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the co-localization of Pol II clusters with the actively transcribed β-actin gene.

claim: The observation of short-lived clusters is not consistent with elongating polymerases.
source: Our observation of short-lived clusters is not consistent with elongating polymerases: if Pol II clusters represented elongating polymerases on the gene, we would expect them to last several minutes on the β-actin gene since each Pol II molecule takes several minutes to transcribe a single mRNA.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the known time required for transcription elongation.

claim: Due to the low photo-conversion rate, the live-cell super-resolution assay may be blind to the smaller number of polymerases actively elongating throughout the gene.
source: To estimate the number of Pol II molecules in a cluster, we considered a limitation in the live cell super-resolution that can be addressed in fixed cells: due to the low photo-conversion rate, our live-cell super-resolution assay may be blind to the smaller number of polymerases actively elongating throughout the gene (scheme in Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a technical limitation of the method, inferred from the principles of the imaging approach.

claim: Clusters may disassemble faster than it would take the live cell super-resolution method to photo-convert and detect all the molecules present in a cluster.
source: In particular, clusters may disassemble faster than it would take the live cell super-resolution method to photo-convert and detect all the molecules present in a cluster.
evidence: This is a technical limitation inferred from the dynamics of the clusters and the method's detection rate.

claim: Chemically fixing the cells may reveal two populations of co-localizing Pol II molecules: a population with smaller number of polymerases attributable to elongating Pol II, and a second population of Pol II clusters that are numerically bigger and distinct from elongating Pol II.
source: We therefore reasoned that chemically fixing the cells may reveal two populations of co-localizing Pol II molecules: a population with smaller number of polymerases attributable to elongating Pol II, and a second population of Pol II clusters that are numerically bigger and distinct from elongating Pol II.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors to address the technical limitation.

claim: Plotting the cumulant graphs of Pol II co-localized with gene loci from 34 fixed cells shows a clear separation between clusters with large counts of detections and those with smaller counts of detections.
source: Plotting the cumulant graphs of Pol II co-localized with gene loci from 34 fixed cells shows a clear separation between clusters with large counts of detections (red in Figure 3D, presumed as clusters large enough for short-lived detection in live cells) and those with smaller counts of detections (gray in Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The hidden-Markov approach successfully converged for the cumulant graphs with small counts of detections and obtained estimates ranging from 1 to 20 molecules.
source: This approach successfully converged for the cumulant graphs (gray in Figure 3D) with small counts of detections and we obtained estimates ranging from 1 to 20 molecules.
evidence: The claim is based on the computational analysis of the data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The hidden-Markov approach failed to converge in finite time due to the large number of molecules for the bigger Pol II clusters.
source: However, the hidden-Markov approach failed to converge in finite time due to the large number of molecules for the bigger Pol II clusters (red in Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a description of a technical limitation of the computational method.

claim: An alternative simulation approach gave a range of 2–22 for the elongating polymerases, in good agreement with the hidden-Markov approach.
source: This approach gave a range of 2–22 for the elongating polymerases, in good agreement with the hidden-Markov approach and consistent with the number of elongating polymerases previously reported for serum stimulated β-actin gene loci (Lionnet et al., 2011a; Femino et al., 1998; Kalo et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by the simulation results and citations to published work (Lionnet et al., 2011a; Femino et al., 1998; Kalo et al., 2015).

claim: The simulation approach successfully approximated the large clusters to be on average ~80 Dendra2-Pol II molecules.
source: The approach successfully approximated the large clusters to be on average ~80 Dendra2-Pol II molecules.
evidence: The claim is based on the simulation results.

claim: A correlation was observed between the smaller Pol II accumulations and the corresponding number nascent RNAs instantaneously detected at the gene locus.
source: In addition we observed a correlation between the smaller Pol II accumulations and the corresponding number nascent RNAs instantaneously detected at the gene locus (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H), while the correlation breaks down for the larger clusters.
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The short-lived clusters observed on the β-actin gene loci are transient agglomerations of ~80 polymerases, which are distinct from the much lower counts of elongating polymerases.
source: We conclude based on the fixed cell co-localization data that the short-lived clusters observed on the β-actin gene loci are transient agglomerations of ~80 polymerases, which are distinct from the much lower counts of elongating polymerases.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the quantitative analysis of fixed cell data.

claim: The β-actin gene is known to display a stereotypical transcription pulse, with a peak output around 15 min after serum stimulation.
source: The β-actin gene is known to display a stereotypical transcription pulse, with a peak output around 15 min after serum stimulation (Lionnet et al., 2011a; Kalo et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Lionnet et al., 2011a; Kalo et al., 2015).

claim: The apparent lifetime of Pol II clusters on the β-actin gene loci increases when observed in the interval between 10 and 15 min, compared to other periods after serum stimulation.
source: We found that the apparent lifetime of Pol II clusters on the β-actin gene loci increases when observed in the interval between 10 and 15 min, compared to other periods after serum stimulation (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Imaging the same cell caused significant fluorescence photo-bleaching of both Pol II and the mRNA signals within a few minutes.
source: Unfortunately, however, imaging the same cell caused significant fluorescence photo-bleaching of both Pol II and the mRNA signals within a few minutes.
evidence: This is a description of a technical limitation encountered in the experiments.

claim: The transcriptional activation of the β-actin gene in MEF cells after serum starvation has a well-characterized stereotyped response that remains evident after averaging multiple cells.
source: The transcriptional activation of the β-actin gene in MEF cells after serum starvation has a well-characterized stereotyped response that remains evident after averaging multiple cells (Lionnet et al., 2011a; Femino et al., 1998; Oleynikov and Singer, 2003; Kalo et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Lionnet et al., 2011a; Femino et al., 1998; Oleynikov and Singer, 2003; Kalo et al., 2015).

claim: Upon serum stimulation, Pol II cluster lifetime increases 3 to 4-fold from a basal lifetime of ~6.9 s, to an average peak lifetime of 24 ± 3 s (at 12.5 min after stimulation), before relaxing back to the basal lifetime.
source: We find that upon serum stimulation, Pol II cluster lifetime increases 3 to 4-fold from a basal lifetime of ~6.9 s, to an average peak lifetime of 24 ± 3 s (at 12.5 min after stimulation), before relaxing back to the basal lifetime (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the quantitative data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The mRNA synthesis burst peaks (around 15 min after serum stimulation) with an average of 18 ± 3 nascent transcripts per gene locus, before decreasing back to the basal loading level of ~4 to 5 transcripts.
source: As represented in Figure 5B, we find that the mRNA synthesis burst peaks (around 15 min after serum stimulation) with an average of 18 ± 3 nascent transcripts per gene locus, before decreasing back to the basal loading level of ~4 to 5 transcripts.
evidence: The claim is supported by the quantitative data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The burst response to serum stimulation, including the peak time and the counts of nascent mRNAs, is in agreement with previous studies of β-actin gene output.
source: The burst response to serum stimulation, including the peak time and the counts of nascent mRNAs, is in agreement with previous studies of β-actin gene output (Femino et al., 1998; Lionnet et al., 2011a; Kalo et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published work (Femino et al., 1998; Lionnet et al., 2011a; Kalo et al., 2015).

claim: The number of Pol II molecules per cluster remained unchanged throughout serum response.
source: We estimated the number of Pol II molecules per cluster as a function of time after serum addition, and it remained unchanged throughout serum response (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A constant frequency of clustering events corresponding to ~0.2 detected clusters per minute remains unchanged up to an hour after serum stimulation.
source: In addition to observing a flat cluster strength, we also observed a constant frequency of clustering events corresponding to ~0.2 detected clusters per minute, which remains unchanged up to an hour after serum stimulation (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Neither the number of Pol II molecules per clusters, nor the frequency of clustering is modulated in response to serum; only the lifetime of Pol II clusters was modulated in a manner correlated with gene expression output.
source: Taken together, these data indicate that neither the number of Pol II molecules per clusters, nor the frequency of clustering is modulated in response to serum; only the lifetime of Pol II clusters was modulated in a manner correlated with gene expression output.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the analysis of multiple parameters shown in Figure 5 and supplements.

claim: There is an experimentally observable delay between Pol II cluster peak (around 12.5 min after stimulation) and mRNA output peak (around 15 min after stimulation).
source: We note that there is an experimentally observable delay between Pol II cluster peak (around 12.5 min after stimulation) and mRNA output peak (around 15 min after stimulation).
evidence: This is an observation from the time-course data in Figure 5A and 5B.

claim: The delay (Δt) between Pol II cluster peak and mRNA output peak is consistent with the expected delay between Pol II recruitment and transcription the MS2 sequence ~3.4 kilobase pairs from the transcription start site of the β-actin gene.
source: This delay (Δt) is consistent with the expected delay between Pol II recruitment and transcription the MS2 sequence ~3.4 kilobase pairs from the transcription start site of the β-actin gene.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known genomic structure and transcription kinetics.

claim: For the data comprising the β-actin gene response to serum (i.e. the first 30 min after serum stimulation), a direct, linear correlation is observed between Pol II cluster lifetime and the number of nascent mRNA subsequently synthesized.
source: For the data comprising the β-actin gene response to serum (i.e. the first 30 min after serum stimulation), we observe a direct, linear correlation between Pol II cluster lifetime and the number of nascent mRNA subsequently synthesized (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the correlation analysis shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Pol II cluster lifetime is directly correlated with the number of nascent mRNAs observed after an apparent lag time Δt.
source: In conclusion, we observe that Pol II cluster lifetime is directly correlated with the number of nascent mRNAs observed after an apparent lag time Δt.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the correlation analysis.

claim: The model yields a best fit Pol II elongation rate of ~3.1 kbp/min, in good agreement with previous publications.
source: The model yields a best fit Pol II elongation rate of ~3.1 kbp/min, in good agreement with previous publications (3–4 kb/min (Singh and Padgett, 2009); ~3 kb/min (Wada et al., 2009; Guo and Price, 2013); 1~6 kb/min (Ardehali and Lis, 2009); 3.6 kbp/min (Fuchs et al., 2014); 1.8 kbp/min, (Jonkers et al., 2014); ~1.5 kbp/min (Veloso et al., 2014)).
evidence: The claim is supported by the model fitting results and citations to published work.

claim: The lag time obtained in the model is Δt = 2 min, compared to the experimentally observed Δt = 2.5 min.
source: The lag time obtained in the model is Δt = 2 min, compared to the experimentally observed Δt = 2.5 min.
evidence: The claim compares the model prediction to the experimental observation.

claim: A relatively simple input-output mechanism can account for the experimental observations.
source: Nevertheless, these model results suggest that a relatively simple input-output mechanism can account for our experimental observations.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the agreement between the model and experimental data.

claim: Flavopiridol, a drug that blocks promoter escape, also stabilizes Pol II clusters.
source: Previously, we found that flavopiridol, a drug that blocks promoter escape, also stabilizes Pol II clusters (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), suggesting a plausible way by which we could control the clustering process (Cisse et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and cited work (Cisse et al., 2013).

claim: DRB prevents the ATP-binding in CDK9, and thereby maintains initiating Pol II in the promoter-proximal paused state.
source: DRB (as well as flavopiridol) prevents the ATP-binding in CDK9, and thereby maintains initiating Pol II in the promoter-proximal paused state (Bensaude, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published work (Bensaude, 2011).

claim: DRB induces stable Pol II clusters analogous to those observed after flavopiridol treatment.
source: Indeed, we observed that DRB induces stable Pol II clusters analogous to those observed after flavopiridol treatment (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Blocking Pol II-loading with one paused polymerase near the promoter by drug treatment leads to a gradual decrease in nascent mRNA count.
source: We expect that blocking Pol II-loading with one paused polymerase near the promoter by drug treatment will lead to a gradual decrease in nascent mRNA count.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the mechanism of action of the drug.

claim: The suppression in the β-actin gene expression profile is observed with both DRB or flavopiridol treatment.
source: We indeed observe this suppression in the β-actin gene expression profile with both DRB or flavopiridol treatment (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Minutes after the β-actin signal disappeared, drug-treated cells featured Pol II clustering exactly at the position where β-actin gene loci were observed.
source: Minutes after the β-actin signal disappeared, drug-treated cells featured Pol II clustering exactly at the position where we observed β-actin gene loci (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D,E.

claim: The observation that Pol II clusters exist at the gene locus, in the absence mRNA synthesis after DRB or flavopiridol treatments, validates the earlier conclusion that Pol II clusters are distinct from elongating polymerase.
source: The observation that Pol II clusters exist at the gene locus, in the absence mRNA synthesis after DRB or flavopiridol treatments, validates our earlier conclusion that Pol II clusters are distinct from elongating polymerase.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the drug treatment experiments.

claim: The Pol II clusters on the β-actin gene loci, after drug treatment, show evidence of stable clusters, with cumulant graphs featuring a slope onset from the beginning of acquisition followed by a more gradual plateau.
source: We note that the Pol II clusters on the β-actin gene loci, after drug treatment, show evidence of stable clusters, with cumulant graphs featuring a slope onset from the beginning of acquisition followed by a more gradual plateau (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D,E.

claim: Drug treatment stabilized Pol II clustering, consistent with previous data on Pol II clusters after drug treatment in human cells.
source: This observation suggests that drug treatment stabilized Pol II clustering, and is consistent with our previous data on Pol II clusters after drug treatment in human cells (Cisse et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison to previous work (Cisse et al., 2013).

claim: A second burst increase in β-actin mRNA synthesis is observed after DRB removal.
source: Consistent with this prediction, we observe a second burst increase in β-actin mRNA synthesis after DRB removal (Figure 6C and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 6C and the source data.

claim: The second burst of transcripts peaks at a time strictly dependent on when DRB is washed.
source: We find that this second burst of transcripts peaks at a time strictly dependent on when we wash DRB (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F–I and Figure 6—source data 1); thus gene bursting is induced at will in a manner that correlates with the presence of a Pol II cluster at the gene locus.
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1F–I and the source data.

claim: The second burst appears long after the normal cellular response to serum was expected to return to the basal mRNA count.
source: In addition, the second burst appears long after the normal cellular response to serum was expected to return to the basal mRNA count (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F–I).
evidence: The claim is supported by the data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1F–I.

claim: Pol II clustering can drive or override the cell's stereotypical response.
source: This observation implies that Pol II clustering can drive or override the cell's stereotypical response.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that the second burst occurs outside the normal response window.

claim: The control of cluster dynamics wields a predictable control of a gene's transcriptional output in live mammalian cells.
source: Nonetheless, these results corroborate our findings that the control of cluster dynamics wields a predictable control of a gene's transcriptional output in live mammalian cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the drug treatment experiments.

claim: Transient Pol II clusters are captured at the loci of actively transcribed β-actin gene in live MEFs.
source: We captured transient Pol II clusters at the loci of actively transcribed β-actin gene in live MEFs.
evidence: This is a summary of the main experimental finding.

claim: The data suggest a transcription regulation mechanism whereby the number of nascent mRNA synthesized is directly correlated with the lifetime of Pol II clusters.
source: Our data suggest a transcription regulation mechanism whereby the number of nascent mRNA synthesized is directly correlated with the lifetime of Pol II clusters.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the correlation analysis.

claim: The clusters normally occur on the active gene locus during transcription initiation, with a basal average lifetime of ~8 s for β-actin, giving rise to a basal mRNA loading level of ~4 nascent transcripts per allele.
source: The clusters normally occur on the active gene locus during transcription initiation, with a basal average lifetime of ~8 s for β-actin, giving rise to a basal mRNA loading level of ~4 nascent transcripts per allele.

claim: Upon stimulation, only the lifetime (and not the size nor the frequency) of Pol II clusters is increased.

evidence: This is a summary of the findings on which parameter changes upon stimulation.

claim: The longer lifetime during initiation gives rise to a proportional increase in the number of Pol II molecules loaded onto the gene.
source: The longer lifetime during initiation gives rise to a proportional increase in the number of Pol II molecules loaded onto the gene.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation between cluster lifetime and mRNA output.

claim: The model suggests that during a clustering event, multiple Pol II molecules are loaded on the gene at a rate of one productive Pol II every 2.5 s.
source: The model suggests that during a clustering event, multiple Pol II molecules are loaded on the gene at a rate of one productive Pol II every 2.5 s.
evidence: This is a parameter obtained from the theoretical model fitting.

claim: With an estimated elongation rate of ~3 kb/min, the loading rate translates into a Pol II packing density of one Pol II complex every ~130 bp, a value close to the maximum density set by the holoenzyme footprint.
source: With an estimated elongation rate of ~3 kb/min, this loading rate translates into a Pol II packing density of one Pol II complex every ~130 bp, a value close to the maximum density set by the holoenzyme footprint (Perry et al., 2010; Kwak and Lis, 2013; Fazal et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the model parameters, with citations to support the maximum density (Perry et al., 2010; Kwak and Lis, 2013; Fazal et al., 2015).

claim: How Pol II clustering is induced, and what controls the dynamics of clustering is currently unknown.

claim: Spatiotemporal clustering of enzymatic factors, through the transient increase of local densities in vivo, are able to effect maximum enzymatic efficiency in a locus-specific manner and when needed.
